TOLLROAD.quote: we have very consciously moved to match the competitors on the minimum order value of Rs. 99

LOWPRICE.rationale: Across all four calls management pairs an explicit affordability/value proposition (free delivery, MOV cut 149→99, value-led pricing mix) with an itemised cost culture — wastage reduction, tight supply-chain cost control, productivity gains, and capex per store down ~20% for three years running — while defending returns through volume and operating leverage.
LOWPRICE.quote: our capex per store has actually reduced year-on-year, and almost nearly 3 years in a row by 20%

PRICING.rationale: Only 'calibrated' price increases on select products (Volcano Pizza) plus premium-mix launches lifted gross margin ~80bps over six months, but this sits against 2.5 years of no hikes, free delivery and a deliberate MOV cut that reduced average order value — value-led deflation coexists with narrow pockets of pricing.
PRICING.quote: we undertook calibrated price increases on select products... The average order value dropped because we have very consciously moved to match the competitors

BRAND.rationale: Domino's shows brand pull — share gains confirmed by an independent Nielsen panel, plans to 'invest more in brand building', and multi-brand stretch (Popeyes, Dunkin, Hong's) — but the flagship brands are licensed rather than owned heritage, and pricing premium is absent; the new brands are currently a profit drag.
BRAND.quote: we have gained share materially in pizza as a category. This allows us to... invest more in brand building

INNOVATION.rationale: A regular, named, margin-accretive product cadence is clearly evidenced every quarter (Big Big Pizza, Chicken Burst, Sourdough, Cheese Lava Pull Apart, Flavor Burst burgers, Cheezilla) alongside AI/tech investment, but there is no disclosed R&D spend or share-of-industry-R&D — this is menu and tech innovation, not R&D-led dominance.
INNOVATION.quote: Sourdough Pizza and Cheese Lava Pull Apart, have seen an overwhelming response and have scaled rapidly... these products are accretive to gross margin

FORWARD.rationale: JFL is a store operator moving customers onto its own digital assets — 15mn MAU app, growing share of own-channel orders, own delivery fleet and 20-minute delivery, plus monetising that traffic with advertising — but it is a franchisee of others' brands rather than a manufacturer integrating forward, and it funds its own store growth rather than franchising it out.
FORWARD.quote: rapidly grown the share of our own digital assets, made decisive progress towards 20-minute delivery

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Explicit, repeated and third-party-corroborated share gain: eight consecutive quarters of positive Domino's India LFL, growth 'ahead of the market', ~230–250 store adds a year taking the network past 3,600 across 500 cities, with a 50,000-customer Nielsen panel confirming category share gains — though gains are partly bought with free delivery and a lower MOV.
SHAREGAIN.quote: there is one truth that Domino's has gained share... a separate panel of 50,000 customers run by Nielsen. They are also indicating that we have gained share

CULTURE.rationale: Within the window management made specific promises and visibly delivered them — the gross-margin improvement flagged 'three or four earnings calls ago' arrived, and the Turkey acquisition debt moved from 'next quarter we will start funding' to being fully serviced by internal cash flows — and it names its own problem areas (dine-in/takeaway, AOV drop, new-brand drag) rather than burying them; long-tenured promoter family remains engaged, but the one-year lens gives limited evidence of behaviour through a downturn.
CULTURE.quote: we had actually mentioned, if you recall in our earnings call about 3 or 4 earnings calls ago that we'll improve the gross margin... that bit has happened

MOATTEST.rationale: Real but not un-replicable barriers: a 2,500+ store Domino's network across 500 cities with commissary supply chain, an owned rider fleet enabling 20-minute delivery, and a 40mn-member digital base — density a new entrant would take years to build — yet management itself flags that 'competition has changed' and had to match rivals on minimum order value, which is not the behaviour of an unassailable position.
MOATTEST.quote: there is competition that has changed... we have very consciously taken a call to reduce minimum order value from Rs.149 to Rs. 99

RECURRING.rationale: The four calls describe volume-based chemical/CDMO supply; there is no discussion of licence fees, AMC/service contracts, attach rates, renewals or customer advances funding the business.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Nothing in the last-12-months calls describes a prescriber/installer channel — sales are direct key-account engagements with innovator customers, and no intermediary economics are discussed either way.

TOLLROAD.rationale: CDMO/fine-chemical molecules are validated into innovators' processes with heavy qualification barriers (USFDA audit of Bharuch, 20+ customer quality/EHS audits cleared in Q1 FY27), which is toll-road-like stickiness; but there is no evidence the product is a trivial share of customer cost, and repeated pricing pressure through Q2–Q3 FY26 argues against non-negotiated pricing.
TOLLROAD.quote: We successfully cleared over 20 customer quality and EHS audits during the quarter

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is a visible, itemised cost culture — a Rs.100 crore/annum lean programme that over-delivered at Rs.120 crore in FY26 and is re-targeted for FY27, power & fuel down 16% y-o-y on 28% renewable share — used explicitly to absorb price falls; but this is cost defence in a commodity/specialty mix, not a low-price-plus scale model with high asset turns.
LOWPRICE.quote: we achieved Rs. 120 crore lean savings

PRICING.rationale: Three of the four calls describe price deflation the company could not resist — 'softer pricing across all 3 segments' in Q3 FY26 — and the Q4 FY26/Q1 FY27 improvement is explicitly crude-linked input-cost pass-through, not price rises above cost inflation.
PRICING.quote: pricing has firmed up due to higher crude linked costs and effective pass-through to customers

BRAND.rationale: No heritage story, A&P spend, distributor leverage or branded adjacency launches are discussed anywhere in the last-12-months calls — the disclosure is entirely B2B volume, molecule and margin commentary.

INNOVATION.rationale: The pipeline is named and quantified each quarter and converts — 100+ opportunities worth ~Rs.3,500 crore peak revenue, confirmed molecules rising 10 → 16 → 20+ → 25+ across the four calls, 20 personal-care products under development, plus dedicated semicon R&D/clean room at Greater Noida; but R&D spend is never disclosed as a number or share, and gross margins are not the high, innovation-funded kind.
INNOVATION.quote: a funnel of 100-plus molecules with INR3,500-plus crore of peak revenue potential with now 25-plus confirmed molecules

FORWARD.rationale: No own stores, franchising, licensing or D2C is mentioned; the only channel move discussed is the Remidex acquisition into premixes, which is an adjacent B2B product step rather than forward integration toward an end consumer.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Share gain is claimed repeatedly and in the tough part of the cycle — domestic and global share growth in Chemical Intermediates despite pricing pressure, and explicit acetyls share gains in Europe aided by competitor force majeure and plant closures — but no share percentages are ever given, so the claim cannot be tracked as a number.
SHAREGAIN.quote: Acetyls improved volumes and pricing with market share gains in Europe

CULTURE.rationale: Within the window the promises made are then delivered: the Oct 2025 'major CDMO order in early 2026' became the Q4 FY26 commencement of the large agro contract; the Rs.100 crore lean target became Rs.120 crore; Bharuch CDMO was built in 14 months; net debt fell 11% to 0.99x EBITDA while dividends were paid, and pricing weakness and the one-off labour-code charge were disclosed plainly rather than buried.
CULTURE.quote: we commissioned Bharuch CDMO plant in record 14 months, reflecting strong execution

MOATTEST.rationale: Parts of the portfolio have a real replication barrier — customer-audited, regulator-inspected CDMO assets and multi-year molecule qualification that a funded newcomer cannot shortcut — but the acetyls/intermediates half is price-taking commodity exposure where margins moved with crude and European closures, so no single articulable barrier protects the whole business.
MOATTEST.quote: successful USFDA audit of our Bharuch site are testament to the world-class infrastructure

RECURRING.rationale: The four calls discuss segment revenue, EBITDA and capex but never attach rates, AMC/service revenue share, renewal rates or deferred revenue/customer advances as a funding source.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Products (allergenic extracts, radiopharmaceuticals) are inherently prescriber-mediated, but the recent calls contain no discussion of channel/professional training, prescriber relationships or how the specialist drives the choice.

TOLLROAD.rationale: Niche critical-supplier traits appear — sole supplier of venom immunotherapy extracts, and CDMO complex-biologics work described as creating high switching costs — but the calls never quantify the product as a tiny share of customer cost, and supply outages (SPECT, isotopes, Montreal) show the position is fragile rather than a rational toll.
TOLLROAD.quote: they create high switching costs and there is more value with these high complex biologics

LOWPRICE.rationale: Cost programmes are discussed (Rs 100 Crore identified, plus a further Rs 50 Crore in the Feb 2023 call), but as turnaround cost-cutting in a loss-making Generics unit, not as a scale-driven low-price-plus model; the calls say nothing about passing savings to price or asset turns.
LOWPRICE.quote: the Company has identified annual savings of Rs 100 Crore in operating costs

PRICING.rationale: There are isolated instances of price capture — better allergy prices in Q3FY23 and a stated premium on complex biologics on line 3 in the May 2026 call — but FY2026 EBITDA margin fell 99bps to 15.9% and Q4 fell 272bps, so pricing is not visibly outrunning cost inflation across the group.
PRICING.quote: we are commanding price premium for these products

BRAND.rationale: No heritage narrative, A&P spend, distributor leverage or brand-adjacency discussion in any of the recent calls; the business is described in B2B capability terms (facilities, compliance, capacity).

INNOVATION.rationale: There is a real proprietary pipeline (JBI-802 and JBI-778 with US FDA orphan drug designations) plus new SPECT/PET/MIBG launches and a discovery business growing 15% to over Rs 650 Crore in FY2026, but R&D spend is never disclosed or sized against the industry, and the novel-drug work is pre-revenue.
INNOVATION.quote: our discovery business grew 15% to now north of Rs. 650 Crores

FORWARD.rationale: The company manufactures radiopharmaceuticals and owns the downstream dispensing network — 46 radiopharmacies, with six new PET pharmacies flagged as a Vision-2030 driver — which is genuine forward integration, though there is no franchising, royalty or D2C economics disclosed.
FORWARD.quote: the second largest network of over 46 Radiopharmacies

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Management claims strong positions (second-largest US allergenic extracts player, sole venom supplier, second-largest radiopharmacy network) and an intent to keep gaining US allergy share, but no explicit share percentages rising over time are given, and FY2026 radiopharma revenue was constrained by supply shortages.
SHAREGAIN.quote: we've been gaining strength in US market and we'd like to continue to gain share in the US market

CULTURE.rationale: Promises from earlier calls were visibly delivered — the Generics and radiopharmacy turnarounds, net debt/EBITDA down from 2.9x to 1.4x, 5 of 6 facilities VAI-compliant — and bad news (Montreal under-absorption, SPECT shortage, FDA observations) is disclosed plainly by a founding family; against that sits notable churn in MD/Chairman roles across FY2024–FY2026 and an FY30 margin target of 23–25% versus 15.9% actually delivered in FY2026.
CULTURE.quote: we have transformed really the Generics business and the Radiopharmacy business, both of them were not doing very well and we have really turned it around

MOATTEST.rationale: Some articulable replication barriers exist — a six-hour-half-life radiopharmacy logistics network, sole-source venom extracts, and FDA-cleared isolator fill-finish lines whose customers face high switching costs — but the same calls show the position is supply- and compliance-dependent (Montreal, SPECT, USFDA observations) rather than structurally uncatchable.
MOATTEST.quote: the half-life on technetium-99 is six hours. So, you can imagine we have to run a really effective supply chain here, and that's at a premium

RECURRING.rationale: Paid campaigns are prepaid subscription contracts: deferred revenue is discussed every quarter as the funding base (INR472.7cr Jan-24 → INR508cr Apr-24 → INR558cr Apr-25, ~90% current), with monthly direct-debit collections and revenue recognised as service is rendered — a customer-funded, negative-working-capital installed base of ~613,000 active campaigns.
RECURRING.quote: Deferred revenue stood at INR558 crores as on March '25 and was up about 10% year-on-year

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Monetisation is a direct telesales relationship with the merchant who both chooses and pays; the recent shift is from cold-calling to advertising-generated qualified leads, with no professional intermediary, installer or prescriber channel anywhere in the four calls.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: we have almost eliminated our cold calling telesales team

TOLLROAD.rationale: The product is a very small line item for an SME (INR1,100/month in Tier 2-3, INR2,200-2,300 in Tier 1, described by the CFO as 'very cheap') yet feeds their lead flow, but management offers no certification, standards or non-switching language to support the toll-road lock-in.
TOLLROAD.quote: I am only at about INR1,100 odd per campaign per month, which is very cheap

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is a genuine, itemised cost culture across all four calls — headcount rationalisation of the bottom 10-20% of sales, automation replacing non-sales manpower, advertising cut ~10-12% YoY to ~INR5cr/quarter — driving EBITDA margin from 10.2% (FY23) to 29.4% (FY25); but the cost work is margin harvesting on a slowing top line rather than scale passed back to customers as price.
LOWPRICE.quote: Employee expenses were only marginally up 0.9% Y-o-Y... 29.8% EBITDA margin

PRICING.rationale: Realisations rose 10.2%, 7.2% and 5.7% YoY across the window and Tier 2-3 pricing has climbed from 40-42% to 48-49% of Tier 1, with FY26 explicitly resting on 'adequate price increases in underpriced categories'; but this is catch-up pricing off a low base, and campaign volume growth decelerated to 5.1% while collections growth fell to 6-7% for three quarters, so pricing is not yet demonstrably volume-neutral.
PRICING.quote: also via adequate price increases in underpriced categories and geographies

BRAND.rationale: Traffic grew to 191.3mn quarterly unique users (+11.8%) on advertising of only ~INR5-7cr a quarter, implying real unaided pull, but management cut A&P deliberately for three of the four quarters and offers no heritage, premium-pricing or adjacency narrative — brand is an input to lead generation, not a stated moat.
BRAND.quote: about 12% lesser advertising on a year-on-year basis

INNOVATION.rationale: New initiatives were explicitly shelved: no capitalisation of development spend for the entire year, no named product launches with revenue impact, no R&D disclosure, and the stated strategy is to keep the core local-search business throwing off cash.
INNOVATION.quote: we don't think there is a significant merit in putting money to just scale up transactions there. So the focus continues to be on the core business

FORWARD.rationale: The calls contain no discussion of own stores, franchising, licensing or D2C logistics — the business model is not manufacturer-to-customer, so the evidence is silent rather than contradictory.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Listings (48.8mn, +11.9%) and traffic are disclosed, but management never gives market-share figures, never names or compares against competitors, and never discusses international expansion — there is no share evidence either way.

CULTURE.rationale: Management owns its misses plainly ('top line growth could have been better... we fell a bit short' on the mid-teens target) and leadership is stable (founder Mani as MD/CEO, Bansal CFO FY21-FY25) with a fortress balance sheet, but the unaddressed INR5,279cr cash pile — including an unutilised INR2,000cr promoter infusion from 2021 — is a long-running capital-allocation failure that analysts raised for '10-15 quarters' before a dividend policy was even promised.
CULTURE.quote: it has been more than 10-15 quarters minority shareholders keep asking you on this call for a better utilization of this huge cash pile

MOATTEST.rationale: The 48.8mn-listing database and 191mn quarterly users are a real accumulated asset, but management never articulates why a well-funded entrant could not rebuild it, and the calls show no time-, capital- or location-based barrier — only cost discipline and price catch-up.
MOATTEST.quote: Total listings now stand at 48.8 million, growing 11.9% year-on-year

RECURRING.rationale: Across all four FY26 calls the revenue discussion is entirely order-book/tender driven (INR5,972cr falling to INR4,675cr); there is no mention of AMC, service contracts, spares attach rates, renewals or customer advances as a funding source.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Sales are direct to Indian Railways, private wagon lessors (GATX), and industrial customers (GE, TMEIC, Tata Solar, Reliance); the EV dealership build-out is a distribution channel, not a professional prescriber who chooses on the customer's behalf. No evidence either way on trade training or specifier lock-in.

TOLLROAD.rationale: The component businesses show toll-road traits — RDSO approval for the Stone India freight brake system and Indian Railways approvals for LHB wheelsets are certification gates that anchor supply — but a wagon or wheelset is a core capex item for the buyer, not a <1-2% input, and pricing is set by tender, so the classic 'pay without negotiating' economics are absent.
TOLLROAD.quote: received RDSO approval for its freight brake system

LOWPRICE.rationale: No cost-culture language, itemised savings or no-frills positioning appears in any of the four calls; margin commentary is about volume and mix, not a structural cost advantage.

PRICING.rationale: Pricing is externally determined — management says tender timing and terms are 'an Indian Railways decision', and the only margin improvement cited was mix shift toward private customers, not price increases; FY26 EBITDA margin fell to 12.4% with no discussion of raising price.
PRICING.quote: honestly, it is an Indian Railways decision as to when they come out with the tender. It is not something which we control

BRAND.rationale: B2B engineering supplier with no heritage story, A&P spend, distributor leverage or premium-pricing claim discussed; the JEM consumer-facing EV brand is too new (first showroom June 2025, ~50 vehicles dispatched) for the calls to say anything about brand strength.

INNOVATION.rationale: Regular named product launches with order impact across FY26 — 10ft/20ft containerised BESS, liquid-cooled grid-scale BESS, in-house BMS/EMS, cell-to-battery line at Indore, RDSO-approved brake system — but no R&D spend is disclosed, gross margins are ordinary (12-13% EBITDA), and there is no claim to a share of industry R&D.
INNOVATION.quote: we launched 10-foot and 20-foot containerized battery energy storage systems with modular air-cooled architecture

FORWARD.rationale: Jupiter Electric Mobility moved to owned retail — first Bengaluru showroom in June 2025 scaling to ~10 dealerships by Nov 2025 with 4-5 more planned — but no store economics, royalty or D2C revenue share is disclosed, and the dominant strategic direction on these calls is backward integration, not forward.
FORWARD.quote: we have close to about 10 dealerships across the country, and we plan to open another four to five

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Named wins in adjacent segments (9,000 LHB axles, 5,376 Vande Bharat wheelsets, long-term Tatravagonka export supply, 110MW BESS) suggest share gain in components and clean energy, but no explicit share percentages are given and the consolidated order book fell every quarter of FY26 from INR5,972cr to INR4,675cr.
SHAREGAIN.quote: given Jupiter's strength and market share

CULTURE.rationale: Bad news is disclosed promptly (wheelset shortage, Q4 LPG/global supply disruption), the promoter converted warrants for INR101.25cr lifting the stake to 68.31%, and the balance sheet stayed conservative at CRISIL AA(-)/stable — but the Q1 guidance of 10-15% growth at 14-15% EBITDA was reaffirmed and then missed (FY26 margin 12.4%), the Odisha partial-production date slipped from Q2 to Q4 FY27 with management framing it as unchanged, and the CFO changed mid-year on top of heavy MD/Chairman churn in FY21-23.
CULTURE.quote: we still maintain our guidelines

MOATTEST.rationale: Real barriers exist — RDSO/Railways approvals, the INR2,500cr Odisha forged wheel and axle plant, and full backward integration across the railroad portfolio — but an analyst on the Feb 2026 call names the Titagarh–RK Forgings JV building the same wheelset capacity, and management concedes availability will normalise once those private capacities arrive, so the advantage is capital-and-time, not un-replicable.
MOATTEST.quote: once these private capacities come online, I don't think there should be any challenges on the availability of wheelsets

RECURRING.rationale: Nothing in the four FY26 calls touches licence fees, AMC/service contracts, subscriptions, attach rates or deferred revenue; the business is one-off sale of FMCG consumables and the topic is simply not discussed.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: No discussion of professionals, installers or prescribers driving demand; the calls describe general trade, modern trade, e-commerce and quick commerce as the routes to a self-selecting consumer, with no trade-training or expert-recommendation angle either way.

TOLLROAD.rationale: The opposite of toll-road economics: the products are visible, substitutable household purchases where rivals cut MRPs and add grammage and Jyothy must follow, and management repeatedly cites 'fixed price points' in low unit packs as a constraint.
TOLLROAD.quote: Competitive intensity remains high with several players reducing MRPs and offering more quantity at the same price.

LOWPRICE.rationale: Prices are falling but returns are falling with them — gross margin down 320bps and EBITDA down 230bps for FY26 — so this is reactive discounting under competitive pressure, not a hard-to-copy cost culture converting low price into high turns and strong returns.
LOWPRICE.quote: Gross margin was 47%, down 320 basis points. EBITDA margin was 15.3%, down by 230 basis points.

PRICING.rationale: Clear price deflation across FY26: volume growth exceeded value growth in every quarter (FY26 6% volume vs 3.5% value; dishwash 6% volume vs -1.3% value), and management says it cannot pass on input inflation in the current demand environment.
PRICING.quote: given the current demand environment, it is difficult to pass on the full impact of cost increases immediately

BRAND.rationale: Real legacy brands (Ujala, Margo, Exo, Pril, Henko, Maxo) with sustained 7-9% A&P and successful stretches — Margo Original/Neem Naturals, Ujala into conditioners and liquids — but the brand does not deliver pricing power, and an analyst pressed management on being stuck in southern markets, so the strength is partial.
BRAND.quote: our A&P spend on a broader time horizon will remain in 8% to 9% range

INNOVATION.rationale: A steady cadence of named launches with disclosed traction — Dr. Wool, Jovia, Ujala Young & Fresh, Maxo Aerosol and rackets, bio-enzyme Exo, and liquid detergents nearly doubling in FY26 — but no R&D spend is disclosed and gross margins fell 320bps, so the innovation is not funding pricing power.
INNOVATION.quote: we strengthened the Exo portfolio with the launch of the bio-enzyme-based dishwash across formats

FORWARD.rationale: No own-store count, franchising, royalties or D2C revenue share is discussed; channel commentary is confined to third-party general trade, modern trade and quick commerce.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Volume consistently ran ahead of the market and category (FY26 fabric care +9.5% volume, Q4 +17.8%; liquids nearly doubled), which implies share gain, but no explicit share numbers vs named competitors are given and much of the gain came via MRP cuts and extra grammage — share bought partly with margin.
SHAREGAIN.quote: Fabric Care delivered strong growth with 14.4% value growth and 17.8% volume growth

CULTURE.rationale: Promises made on earlier calls were delivered — the HI turnaround plan cut losses from INR25cr to about INR5cr and lifted LV to 55% of the mix — alongside a debt-free balance sheet with INR1,000cr cash, working capital improved to 15 days, and open discussion of the loss-making JKBL divestment; judged on one year only, without multi-year corroboration.
CULTURE.quote: losses reduced significantly from INR25 crores last year to about INR5 crores this year

MOATTEST.rationale: Nothing on these calls is un-replicable — competitors freely cut MRPs, raise grammage and compress Jyothy's realisations in its core dishwash and detergent categories, and management concedes quick commerce competition is decided on price because user experience is similar.
MOATTEST.quote: Pricing remains the primary differentiator on these platforms due to similar user experiences.

RECURRING.rationale: Across all four FY26 calls management discusses order book, capacity and execution only; there is no discussion of AMC/service revenue share, attach rates, spares, renewals or customer advances/deferred revenue as a funding source. The single passing reference to 'service supports' carries no economics.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Sales are direct to industrial end-users (aerospace/defence, auto, EMS, general engineering) who both choose and pay; the calls describe wallet-share gains with marquee clients and exhibition-led engagement (EMO Germany), not a prescriber/installer channel.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: have steadily increased our wallet share with marquee clients

TOLLROAD.rationale: A CNC machine tool is a capital-expenditure decision for the buyer, not a sub-1% consumable; the calls show customers negotiating within a competitive import-heavy market (60% of Indian demand still imported) rather than a rational oligopoly with certification-anchored pass-through.
TOLLROAD.quote: nearly 60% of this requirement is still met through imports

LOWPRICE.rationale: Management repeatedly frames vertical integration as delivering global-standard precision at Indian cost, and is building proprietary controllers/drives/motors to cut import dependence — but the economics are high-margin (55.9% gross margin, 25-29% EBITDA), not the low-margin/high-asset-turn model, and no itemised cost culture is evidenced.
LOWPRICE.quote: we do so with precision, reliability, and cost competitiveness suited to global standards

PRICING.rationale: Gross margin rose 270bps to 55.9% in Q1 FY26 and standalone Q4 EBITDA margin reached 31.9%, and with utilisation above 100% management says it is deliberately rationing order intake — scarcity consistent with pricing power — but no call discusses explicit price increases or elasticity, and consolidated FY26 margin fell to 25.2%.
PRICING.quote: we have been considerate in the order booking to match our delivery obligations

BRAND.rationale: Reputation language recurs (top-10 global CNC maker, 'customers of high repute', Huron's standing defended during the export-control probe), but there is no A&P spend, heritage narrative with pricing premium, or measured brand-driven share gain in these calls.
BRAND.quote: Jyoti Huron continued to enjoy a strong reputation across both domestic and international markets

INNOVATION.rationale: FY26 calls name concrete development work — the Huma control panel, planned in-house controllers/drives/motors, and next-generation semiconductor-equipment machines — with Huron as a technology hub, but R&D spend is never disclosed or quantified and no revenue is attributed to named launches.
INNOVATION.quote: initiatives such as the Huma control panel along with plans to integrate proprietary controllers, drives and motors

FORWARD.rationale: The July 2025 Tumakuru land purchase is explicitly to place support centres, technology centres and a warehouse next to EMS customer clusters, and Huron gives owned European manufacturing/assembly presence — customer-proximate control, but no own-store, franchise or D2C economics are disclosed.
FORWARD.quote: the idea is to set up support centers, technological center and a warehouse closer to our customers

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Consolidated revenue grew 15.8% in H1, 28.1% in Q3 and ~19% for FY26 against a largely import-served domestic market, with order book rising from Rs.4,412cr to Rs.4,732cr through the year — directionally share-gaining, but management never cites an actual market-share number or a named competitor comparison.
SHAREGAIN.quote: The Indian CNC machine tools market continued to be largely served through import

CULTURE.rationale: Promoter-led with prompt bad-news disclosure — the Huron export-control investigation and the prudent Rs.67cr POCM revenue reversal were volunteered in the opening remarks, and the Feb 2026 call proactively explained high inventory days; against that, the capacity message shifted between calls (10,000 by Sep-26 in Aug, then 6,000→16,000 from Nov) and FY26 PAT grew only 6%.
CULTURE.quote: based on the assessment of our local auditors for Huron and as a matter of prudence... reversed a revenue amounting to INR67 crores

MOATTEST.rationale: The calls point to genuinely slow-to-replicate assets — decades of in-house R&D, vertical integration, the Huron high-precision French base, and aerospace/defence qualification (41% of order book) — but the Rs.750cr+ capacity build to 16,000 machines is capital a funded entrant could also deploy, and management concedes capacity, not moat, is the binding constraint.
MOATTEST.quote: One of the key challenges we encountered was capacity constraint

RECURRING.rationale: No discussion of licence fees, AMC/service contracts, renewals, attach rates or customer advances funding the business in any of the four calls.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Sales run through dealers/distributors rather than end-consumer transactions, and in Oct 2025 management admitted they had never serviced the architect/influencer channel and only just built an 18-20 person team for it — an ambition, not an established professional-prescriber moat, with no trade training programmes described.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: Coming to architects, influencers, we were never there. We never serviced them.

TOLLROAD.rationale: Management argues tiles are a small line item in a construction budget so end-user demand absorbs price rises, but the calls show the opposite of toll-road pricing discipline — Q3 FY26 required discounts to clear SKUs and dealers churn freely; no certification, standards or switching-cost language appears.
TOLLROAD.quote: Not really. I think the demand is there and tile is a very small segment

LOWPRICE.rationale: A genuine, itemised cost drive is under way — INR150 crores annualised savings from carton re-engineering, ~250 headcount removed, travel and raw-material renegotiation, and a supplier meet — but this is a two-year 'Kajaria 2.0' catch-up programme, not an embedded low-cost culture, and savings are being retained/reinvested in advertising rather than passed to price.
LOWPRICE.quote: During the year, we have achieved cost savings of more than INR 150 crores on an annualised basis.

PRICING.rationale: Q4 FY26 showed 12-13% price increases in North (16-17% Morbi) alongside 11% volume growth, but management framed it as gas-cost pass-through rather than value pricing, and Q3 FY26 realisation fell ~2-2.4% on inventory-liquidation discounts — pricing follows input costs, it does not lead them.
PRICING.quote: more or less we have covered the cost of increase of gas with some added margin

BRAND.rationale: Brand is stretched across Kajaria tiles, Kerovit bathware and Gresbond adhesives with adhesives more than doubling (INR21cr to INR44cr in Q4), and ~INR24 crores of quarterly A&P is disclosed — but FY26 ad spend was cut year-on-year and the brand did not prevent flat tile volumes for three quarters.
BRAND.quote: So overall ad spend in the year would be lower as compared to the last year

INNOVATION.rationale: Innovation shows up only as mix shift — converting a 9.1 msm Gailpur line from ceramic floor tiles to glazed vitrified, plus SKU rationalisation — with no R&D spend, pipeline or named-launch revenue disclosed on any call.
INNOVATION.quote: we have converted 1 unit with a capacity of 9.1 million square meters from ceramic floor tiles to glazed vitrified tiles, to move towards value-added products

FORWARD.rationale: The four calls discuss only the dealer/distributor channel; no own-store counts, franchise royalties, D2C share or e-commerce logistics investment is mentioned either way.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Share gain is an explicit stated objective (a management consultant hired to raise share, dealer white-space mapping) and Q4 FY26 delivered 11% volume growth against a weak market plus Morbi shutdowns, but the preceding three quarters were flat-to-down with no share numbers ever quantified.
SHAREGAIN.quote: we have kept a consultant now, a management consultant, who is guiding us how to increase the market share

CULTURE.rationale: Management convened a dedicated December 2025 call to disclose a fraud at the Kerovit Global step-down subsidiary that its own new controls had surfaced, admitted the earlier lapse plainly ('a lapse on our part... we ignored that'), appointed E&Y as forensic auditor, and stated an explicit disclosure principle; cost-saving and unification promises made in Oct 2025 were visibly delivered by Q4 FY26 under stable family leadership.
CULTURE.quote: This is Kajaria 2.0, where our philosophy is very, very clear. Bad news to be shared immediately and good news only to be shared on completion.

MOATTEST.rationale: The only replication barrier articulated is multi-locational plants plus ~15-30% biofuel mix giving a fuel-cost edge over single-cluster Morbi players — a real but rebuildable advantage, and the year's dealer churn, SKU-clearing discounts and flat volumes show no un-replicable lock-in.
MOATTEST.quote: Kajaria and other players who have multi locational plants will have a great advantage as we go forward

RECURRING.rationale: The four calls discuss showroom revenue, FOCO share and franchise economics, but never license fees, AMC/service contracts, renewal or attach rates, or deferred revenue/customer advances as a funding source, so there is no basis to judge this either way in the last 12 months.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Every demand driver discussed is direct end-consumer: Navratri/Diwali/Akshaya Tritiya footfall, brand campaigns lifting conversions, wedding purchases. No professional prescriber, installer or trade-training channel exists between Kalyan and the buyer.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: Footfalls at the showrooms and conversions have shown more than 75% increase since launch of the brand campaign.

TOLLROAD.rationale: Jewellery is a large discretionary purchase for the end customer, not a sub-1% critical input, and the calls contain no certification, standards or industry-anchoring language; management instead describes managing consumer sensitivity to the gold price.
TOLLROAD.quote: our inventory levels, 18 karat percentage would, we will increase a bit, so that the volume does not get hurt too much

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is a genuine and quantified cost/capital-efficiency culture — the lean-credit procurement pilot worth 0.2–0.3% of gross margin, the capital-light FOCO model, working-capital and debt reduction — but nothing in the four calls about passing savings to customers as lower price or competing on price at all.
LOWPRICE.quote: a key change in the procurement plan for the new format by focusing on a lean credit period, ensuring better cost efficiencies

PRICING.rationale: Value growth held up remarkably through a near-doubling of gold prices (Q4 FY26 revenue +66%, SSSG 30%+), which shows demand resilience to a rising ticket, but management attributes margin gains to procurement and product/region mix rather than its own price increases, and it trims volumes/shifts to 18kt to protect affordability.
PRICING.quote: maybe 0.2%, 0.3% because of the pilot and the rest can be very minimal for other metals like platinum, silver

BRAND.rationale: Brand investment is visible and works — the Candere campaign drove a 75%+ rise in footfall and conversions, and the name is being stretched into new formats and geographies (UK showroom, US/UK pilots) — but the excerpts carry no heritage/provenance story, A&P quantum, or evidence of premium pricing from the brand.
BRAND.quote: We launched the brand campaign for Candere during the current financial year and plan to add 80 Candere showrooms in India this year.

INNOVATION.rationale: No R&D spend, pipeline, named product launches with revenue impact, or share-of-industry-R&D discussion appears in any of the four calls; new formats are retail-format launches, not disclosed innovation economics.

FORWARD.rationale: This is the dominant structural story of the year: capital-light FOCO franchising now at 43% of revenue with 160+ showrooms added over three years, third-party franchisee capital funding growth, 129 launches in FY26 with 150 planned, plus the Candere omnichannel/D2C build (110 stores, revenue +160%, PAT positive from H2 FY26) and overseas own-store pilots.
FORWARD.quote: Over the last 3 years, we have opened more than 160 Kalyan showrooms in India, predominantly through the capital-light FOCO model. Share of FOCO revenue has grown to 43%

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Growth is persistently and far above sector run-rate — FY26 consolidated revenue INR35,740 crores, +43%, SSSG in excess of 30% for the 30 days to Diwali, accelerating non-South share shift, strong franchise sign-ups — and it is not bought with balance-sheet risk, since debt fell INR360 crores in the same year and a dividend was paid from free cash.
SHAREGAIN.quote: same-store sales growth for the 30-day period ending Diwali was in excess of 30% on a like-for-like basis

CULTURE.rationale: Within this 12-month window the promises made on earlier calls were then delivered on later ones: the INR300 crore annual debt-reduction target came in at ~INR360 crores, Candere was promised PAT-neutral/positive by year-end and turned PAT positive in Q3 and for H2, and the collateral-release and dividend-policy commitments were followed through; leadership (Kalyanaraman family, CEO Sanjay Raghuraman since FY2023) is stable and the tone on debt is conservative.
CULTURE.quote: Over the last 3 years, we have reduced the non-GML in India from INR1,300 crores to INR300 crores.

MOATTEST.rationale: What a new entrant would have to replicate is a large franchisee base with balance-sheet depth, regional store density and consumer trust in gold purity — real but capital-and-time barriers rather than un-replicable ones, and management itself concedes it must compete with 'strong regional brands' by creating a separate localized format.
MOATTEST.quote: an entity that will house regional brands offering exclusively localized jewellery, competing with strong regional brands

RECURRING.rationale: No discussion of attach rates, AMC/licence renewals, deferred revenue or customer advances as a funding source in any of the four calls; 'paint as a service' at >5% of decorative is a service add-on, not a disclosed recurring contracted stream.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Sales are pushed through trade professionals rather than end-consumers: the Pragati painter loyalty programme (1 lakh+ painters), an architect/interior-designer programme across 45+ cities with ~8,000 architects onboard, plus body-shop and OEM line engineers in industrial — classic expert-recommends, consumer-pays economics with training-based switching costs.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: we have 1 lakhs+ painters associated with the Pragati Program... almost 8000 architects are almost onboard

TOLLROAD.rationale: The industrial/automotive side has toll-road traits — paint is a small share of a vehicle's cost yet halts the line if it fails, and Nerolac embeds 200–300 technical staff on customer lines with a clean supply/quality record used as the switching barrier. But no explicit '<1-2% of customer cost', certification-standard or oligopoly language, and the majority decorative business is openly price-competitive.
TOLLROAD.quote: we have not faced situations where customers have suffered due to Nerolac's supply or quality issues. That is a strong credential that helps protect our business

LOWPRICE.rationale: Management explicitly positions against the low-price end, saying the bottom-of-the-pyramid players face margin pressure and that its own strategy is premiumisation and selectivity; there is no cost-obsession culture or itemised-savings language in any call.
LOWPRICE.quote: there are players operating at the bottom of the pyramid, where margin pressure is clearly higher. For multinational players like us, the strategy is focused on premiumization

PRICING.rationale: No price increases are described anywhere in the window, and the numbers show the opposite of pricing power: Q3 FY26 net revenue +3.5% with PBDIT +0.2% and PBT before exceptionals -3.7%; 9M net revenue +1.9% with PBT -4%, against 'elevated' competitive intensity and rupee-driven input cost surge.
PRICING.quote: our growth in net revenue was 3.5%. For PBDIT, it was 0.2% and PBT before exceptional items was minus 3.7%

BRAND.rationale: Genuine heritage and sustained A&P — 100-year legacy, a three-decade-old jingle refreshed, Ghar Ki Raunak across TV/Asia Cup/digital — but the brand is self-described as No.2 in equity and is not converting into premium pricing or share gain, which the pattern requires.
BRAND.quote: We proudly hold the position of a second most recognized brand in terms of the brand equity index nationwide

INNOVATION.rationale: Innovation is regular and named — 20+ launches in FY25, 11 new products in FY26, Paint+ now >10% of decorative (up 190bps in a year), plus a steady stream of industrial products (Excel Everlast 20, BTX-free monocoat, low-bake CED) drawn from Kansai Japan technology. What is missing is the profit engine the pattern needs: R&D spend is never quantified, and gross-margin/PBT are falling, so innovation is not yet funding pricing power.
INNOVATION.quote: Paint+ group of products... today, their contribution to overall decorative business is greater than 10%... during the year, we have launched 11 new products

FORWARD.rationale: Real but early forward integration: NXTGEN Shoppe / Shop-in-Shop / Nerolac Plus Paint Zones grew from ~350 to 600+ outlets and paint-as-a-service now runs across 250 cities, yet own-store contribution was only mid-single-digit of decorative and no franchise royalty or D2C revenue economics are disclosed.
FORWARD.quote: Our specialty stores... today, the network is more than 600 plus... Services have continued to grow and are contributing more than 5% to our overall decorative business

SHAREGAIN.rationale: The company is a share loser in its largest segment on its own account — it grew 1.5-1.9% for 9M FY26 while conceding the industry is growing and part of that growth is going to new entrants and smaller players; in decorative it ranks No.3 and is defending, not gaining.
SHAREGAIN.quote: a part of that growth is being captured by smaller players who have recently entered the market, and that is why we see listed companies reporting slightly lower growth rates

CULTURE.rationale: Management discloses bad news plainly (declining PBDIT/PBT, competitive pressure) and keeps investing in R&D, stores and construction-chemical acquisitions, but leadership stability — a core marker — is absent: chairman changed FY25, MD Anuj Jain exited, a new MD, new CFO and a Japan-side director stepped down all within this window, and the promoter's 9-10% growth / 14-15% EBITDA ambition set in Apr 2025 was not being delivered by Feb 2026.
CULTURE.quote: we are aiming for 9% growth on an annual basis EBITDA margin. We will aim for 14%-15% on our road to achieve 18%

MOATTEST.rationale: Management articulates a concrete, time-based replication barrier for industrial coatings — eight plants, 200–300 technicians embedded on customer lines, global track record and approval cycles that money alone cannot shortcut — but explicitly concedes decorative has no such barrier, where a well-funded conglomerate is running 'not very different' a strategy and taking share.
MOATTEST.quote: success is not only about having a ready-made business. It also requires a complete supply chain and value chain setup, strong technology offerings... proven global track records, but all of this takes time

RECURRING.rationale: The calls discuss deposits, fee lines and bancassurance income but never in terms of an upfront product sale followed by a contracted recurring stream — no attach rates, renewal rates, AMC share or deferred-revenue funding language appears.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Although KVB sources mortgages via an 'open market channel' and co-lends with NBFCs, the calls repeatedly show the end borrower is highly price-sensitive — accounts are lost outright on rate, the opposite of the low-price-sensitivity that defines this pattern.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: allowed few accounts to be taken over by others due to lower pricing, which did not fit into scheme of things for our bank

TOLLROAD.rationale: Credit is a large, negotiated share of a borrower's cost base, and the Q3/Q4 FY26 calls describe customers switching lenders purely on price; there is no certification, standards or 'don't switch once converted' language anywhere.
TOLLROAD.quote: Conscious of acquisition of accounts, both in terms of quality and pricing allowed few accounts to be taken over by others due to lower pricing

LOWPRICE.rationale: The bank variant is partly present — cost-to-income held at 43.98% within a sub-50% guided range, CASA growth of INR3,290 crores described as the highest in ten years, and an unsecured book of just 1.81% called one of the lowest among peers — but there is no evidence of a genuinely cheap deposit franchise or an itemised cost-obsession culture, and deposit rates were raised 40bps in Q1 FY27 to fund growth.
LOWPRICE.quote: Our unsecured loan book is at 1.81% of the total advances as at the end of March 2026, which is one of the lowest amongst the peers.

PRICING.rationale: Management defends spreads deliberately — NIM rose from 3.77% (Q2 FY26) to 3.99% and then 4.26% in Q1 FY27, above pre-rate-cut levels despite 125bps of repo cuts, and they walk away from underpriced business — but this is asset-mix and liability repricing discipline, not price increases without volume loss, since holding price costs them accounts and slows commercial growth.
PRICING.quote: Despite the repo rate cut by 125 basis points since February '25, we could improve our NIM over pre-reduction time by effectively calibrating the asset mix and optimizing the yields.

BRAND.rationale: The four calls in the window contain no discussion of heritage, brand investment, A&P spend, distributor leverage or premium positioning — the narrative is entirely balance-sheet, margin and asset-quality metrics.

INNOVATION.rationale: There is a steady cadence of named product and channel launches — GST surrogate and open term loan products, credit card relaunch, loan against mutual funds, and the API-first Transaction Banking Group — but no R&D disclosure, no share-of-industry-innovation claim, and no evidence these drive pricing power.
INNOVATION.quote: Tailor-made products such as GST surrogate for customers with limited financial data and open term loan product started during the last quarter are slowly gaining traction

FORWARD.rationale: Not applicable in the evidence — branch and relationship-manager expansion (mortgage-focused branches from 144 to 175, SBG model across 77 branches) is distribution build-out within a bank's own model, and the calls say nothing about franchising, licensing or own-store economics.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Growth has run well above system credit growth for the whole window — total business +15-16% YoY to INR2,27,267 crores, retail advances +25% and mortgages +56% in FY26, with INR75,000 crores of business added over 3.5 years — but management gives no explicit market-share numbers versus named competitors and deliberately moderated growth in Q4 FY26.
SHAREGAIN.quote: the bank has achieved a significant milestone of reaching INR2 lakh crores in business... the bank has added INR75,000 crores in business over the past 3.5 years

CULTURE.rationale: Across all four calls the same leadership team (Ramesh Babu as MD/CEO with the same ED, COO and CFO) repeats guidance and then delivers on it — NIM guidance of 3.7-3.75% met, INR600 crore recovery guidance met at INR601 crores, cost-to-income within the guided range — and they voluntarily strip a INR139 crore one-off interest recovery out of the reported margin rather than flatter it, while consciously exiting weak and underpriced accounts.
CULTURE.quote: we have excluded this amount for margin calculations in the presentation to give a realistic picture

MOATTEST.rationale: Nothing in the window articulates why a funded competitor could not replicate KVB's position; on the contrary, the Q3 and Q4 FY26 calls describe rivals taking accounts away on price and heightened competition forcing the bank to 'lie low' in housing and vehicle loans.
MOATTEST.quote: Considering the low yields and increased competition, we continue to lie low in housing loans and vehicle loans.

RECURRING.rationale: The four calls discuss order book, project-linked revenue recognition and working capital, but never attach rates, AMC/service revenue share, renewals or customer advances as a funding source.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: No discussion of professionals, installers or prescribers driving demand; sales are direct B2B/OEM contracts. Evidence is silent rather than contradictory.

TOLLROAD.rationale: No language about being a tiny-but-critical share of customer cost, certification/standards anchoring, or customers not switching once converted; the calls frame Kaynes as a contract manufacturer executing customer projects.

LOWPRICE.rationale: Cost and productivity are mentioned only as internal operating discipline (TPM, execution), not as a low-price-plus-scale strategy with itemised savings passed to customers.
LOWPRICE.quote: drive significant improvements in productivity, cost and delivery while embedding a culture of total predictive maintenance across all sites

PRICING.rationale: No price increases, premiumisation, elasticity or waiting-list language in any of the four calls; margin expansion (15.8-16.3% EBITDA) is attributed to mix and integration, not pricing.

BRAND.rationale: No heritage story, A&P spend, distributor leverage or brand-adjacency launches — this is an unbranded B2B manufacturing business.

INNOVATION.rationale: The FY26 calls repeatedly describe a shift from service-led EMS to design-led ESDM, India's first commercially manufactured multichip module at Sanand, and early-stage design engagement on high-end HDI PCBs — but no R&D spend, pipeline economics or share-of-industry-R&D is disclosed, and margins remain mid-teens rather than innovation-grade.
INNOVATION.quote: successfully delivering India's first commercially manufactured multichip module, IPM5 in collaboration with Alpha & Omega Semiconductor and Mitsui & Company

FORWARD.rationale: Management explicitly describes the opposite direction — backward integration into PCB fabrication and OSAT chip packaging — with no own stores, franchising, licensing or D2C.
FORWARD.quote: our PCB manufacturing initiative, a critical element of our backward integration strategy

SHAREGAIN.rationale: FY26 revenue grew 33% with a ~INR90,000mn non-cancellable order book, North American entry via August Electronics and new OSAT/PCB platforms, but no explicit market-share figures versus named competitors, and execution ran ~20% below plan against that order book.
SHAREGAIN.quote: against our plan, there is a shortfall of around 20%

CULTURE.rationale: Genuinely mixed over the window: management convened a dedicated December 2025 call to answer disclosure/accounting criticism, admitted reporting errors, acknowledged missing market expectations, kept debt/equity at ~0.2, and delivered a promised working-capital improvement (core EMS 83 to 53 days) — but the same year featured repeated execution shortfalls, top-management restructuring and a CFO/MD churn record that undercuts the stability leg.
CULTURE.quote: We acknowledge that a few disclosures required clearer clarification and articulation. These were errors in reporting of disclosure in notes to accounts

MOATTEST.rationale: The OSAT and HDI PCB plants carry real replication barriers — ISM/FSA government approval, INR1,500 crore capex, anchor tie-ups with AOS, Infineon and L&T Semiconductor — but the core EMS business that still generates almost all revenue is a contract-assembly activity the calls give no articulable reason a funded entrant could not rebuild.
MOATTEST.quote: A key area of concern for many stakeholders have been the approval of the FSA under the ISM framework for OSAT. I am pleased to confirm that this approval is now in place.

RECURRING.rationale: KEC is a project-based EPC contractor: every call describes lumpy order intake (INR25,280 crores FY26), order book and L1 visibility of 'six to seven quarters', and revenue recognised on execution — no attach rates, AMC/service share, renewals or installed-base density anywhere. Working capital runs the wrong way: net debt including acceptances rose to INR6,806 crores on delayed water collections and spillover receivables, i.e. KEC funds customers, not the reverse.
RECURRING.quote: current order book plus L1 position stands at over INR40,000 crores, which gives us visibility for the next six to seven quarters

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Sales are direct B2B to the paying customer — PGCIL, SEBs, private TBCB developers, Adani, Middle East utilities, real estate developers — won through competitive tendering, not recommended by an intermediary professional. The calls repeatedly describe bidding and L1 positions, the opposite of a specifier-led channel.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: selectively bid for high-quality margin-accretive opportunities in both domestic and international markets

TOLLROAD.rationale: KEC's EPC contracts are the customer's major capital cost item, not a sub-1% critical input, and they are re-tendered project by project with no certification or standards anchoring. No switching-cost or 'don't switch once converted' language appears in any of the four calls.
TOLLROAD.quote: we have an L1 position of over INR6,000 crores

LOWPRICE.rationale: Margins are structurally thin (FY26 EBITDA ~7%, operating PAT margin 2.6%) but that is competitive-tender economics, not a low-price-plus flywheel: the balance sheet is debt-heavy at INR6,722 crores net debt and asset turns are constrained by working capital, and management's stated strategy is fewer/larger higher-quality orders rather than price leadership.
LOWPRICE.quote: we sharpened our focus on enhancing the quality of order inflows by consciously shifting towards fewer but larger EPC orders

PRICING.rationale: Pricing is set by competitive bidding — the company wins by being L1 — and there is no mention of price increases in any of the four calls; margin gains come from mix shift to T&D, interest cost reduction and execution, while cost shocks (war-related freight surcharges, LPG shortages) are absorbed rather than passed through.
PRICING.quote: freight costs, including war-related surcharges have increased materially, particularly for ocean transportation

BRAND.rationale: Reputation functions as a prequalification asset — repeat orders from marquee clients, 15 years of SAE, 'largest ever' orders in Saudi/UAE and the first HVDC converter station commissioned with Adani and Hitachi — but this is credential-based trust in tenders, not consumer brand pricing power, and there is no A&P spend or premium-price evidence.
BRAND.quote: our largest ever EPC order of over INR3,100 crores in the UAE, our largest ever substation order of over INR1,000 crores in Saudi Arabia

INNOVATION.rationale: Capability-building is real and named each quarter — HVDC converter stations (five projects executing), KAVACH/TCAS train protection, ABS signalling, semiconductor EPC entry, e-beam and elastomeric cables for defence/auto/rail — but gross margins are too thin to fund outsized R&D, and no R&D spend figure is disclosed on any call.
INNOVATION.quote: This plant will cater to high-performance applications across defence, automotive and railway sectors where superior durability and thermal resistance are critical

FORWARD.rationale: KEC is already a direct contractor to end-clients with in-house manufacturing (towers at Dubai, Jaipur, Jabalpur, Butibori; cables at Vadodara; SAE in Brazil/Mexico); there are no own stores, franchising, licensing or D2C economics of any kind in the last four calls.
FORWARD.quote: the expansion of our Butibori facility in Nagpur is expected to be completed by March '26

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Evidence points to share gain in T&D — FY26 T&D revenue INR15,883 crores (+24%), international T&D orders +35% with Africa/CIS revival, SAE +36%, record all-time order intake INR25,280 crores, and deliberate scaling into the private TBCB segment (INR3,600 crores from private players/SEBs) — but management never quotes its own market-share percentage or names competitors, and the 75%/80% share figures cited refer to private developers' share of the TBCB market, not KEC's.
SHAREGAIN.quote: the share of these players has increased significantly to almost 80% compared to 45% last year

CULTURE.rationale: Kejriwal (MD since FY2022) and CFO Aggarwal give consistently candid, itemised explanations of shortfalls — labour shortages, water-segment payment delays, LPG/election disruption, INR59 crore labour-code provision, Middle East logistics — and disclose operating vs reported PAT transparently. But the repeatedly promised improvements have not yet landed: 'debt levels to normalize' was said in Nov 2025 and Jan 2026 (targeting March '26), yet Q4 net debt was INR6,722 crores and the promise moved to Q2 FY27, and 'Civil will see good growth in the coming quarters' recurred in all four calls while Civil revenue went INR940cr → INR968cr → INR923cr.
CULTURE.quote: We expect the debt levels to normalize going forward

MOATTEST.rationale: There are genuine, non-trivial barriers — multi-decade global execution track record, prequalification credentials for 765kV/HVDC and GIS substations, owned tower plants across Dubai/India/Brazil/Mexico, and niche certifications like KAVACH — which a funded newcomer could not assemble quickly. Yet the calls also show the barrier eroding at the customer end: six new private players entered TBCB in one year, and KEC still competes tender-by-tender at ~7% EBITDA margins, which is not the return profile of an un-replicable moat.
MOATTEST.quote: six new private players entering the TBCB segment during the year

RECURRING.rationale: Across all four FY26 calls revenue is disclosed purely as one-off product sales — B2C dealer sales, B2B institutional/EHV cable orders, exports, EPC and stainless steel wire — with no license fees, AMC, service attach or renewal stream, and no deferred revenue/customer advances discussed as a funding source (funding came from a Rs.2,000 cr QIP instead).
RECURRING.quote: Sales through distribution network is INR6,349 crores, up by 25%... EPC sales other than cable is INR311 crores

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Over half of sales (54-56%) go through a 2,100+ active dealer network rather than end-customer marketing, and B2C grew 25% in FY26 — but the FY26 calls never describe electrician/contractor training programmes or channel relationship investment that would create professional switching costs.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: The total active working dealers of the company as on 31st March '26 was approximately 2,125. Dealer sales contribution is 54% in overall sales.

TOLLROAD.rationale: Cable is a small but mission-critical line item in solar, data-centre and T&D projects, and the Q3 FY26 call leans on qualification/approval anchoring — sole Indian qualification in the National Grid UK framework to 400 kV and 'gaining acceptance' as an EHV supplier in the Middle East — but no call quantifies the <1-2% of customer cost or non-switching behaviour.
TOLLROAD.quote: KEI is the only Indian company to qualify in National Grid UK framework agreement for maximum voltages up to 400 kV.

LOWPRICE.rationale: The FY26 calls contain no cost-culture language, itemised savings, or no-frills positioning; margin discussion is about mix and commodity pass-through, not a low-price/high-turns model.

PRICING.rationale: Q2 FY26 shows 22% wire & cable value growth of which 15% was volume and the balance price, with retail prices reset every 15 days and price-variation clauses on B2B orders — but management frames this as commodity pass-through that leaves margins unchanged, not price rises above cost inflation; genuine margin expansion (EBITDA 10.92%→11.81% in FY26) came alongside a 16.85% copper cost rise.
PRICING.quote: all the retail segment pricing is revised every 15 days... commodity price goes up and down, but our margins are not impacted

BRAND.rationale: The B2C/retail franchise is clearly working — dealer-channel sales up 29% in Q4 FY26 and 25% for the full year, well ahead of the institutional book — but across all four calls there is no discussion of A&P spend, heritage positioning, premium price realisation versus competitors, or brand-led adjacency launches.
BRAND.quote: Sales through dealer network, distribution network is INR1,936 crores in fourth quarter against INR1,498 crores with a growth of around 29%

INNOVATION.rationale: Technical capability is real and product-specific — electron-beam equipment for solar wires commissioning in April '26, 330 kV supply to Australia, 220 kV to UAE and Spain — but no R&D spend is disclosed or discussed in any FY26 call, and there is no named annual pipeline with revenue impact.
INNOVATION.quote: our electron beam equipment to manufacture, electron beam pure solar wires will be commissioned, and that will add another boost to this plant

FORWARD.rationale: KEI moves downstream through its EHV EPC/turnkey division (Q4 FY26 EHV EPC sales Rs.106 cr vs Rs.32 cr) which controls project delivery to the end customer, but there are no own stores, franchising, royalties or D2C e-commerce — retail reach is entirely through third-party dealers.
FORWARD.quote: Out of the total sales of EPC, extra high-voltage cable EPC sale is INR106 crores against INR32 crores in the same period last year.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: FY26 delivered 20.66% net sales growth (wire & cable 22.32%) with exports up 45% to Rs.1,833 cr and EHV up 82%, plus repeated international qualification wins (National Grid UK, Australia 330 kV, three UAE 132 kV contracts, Caribbean/West Indies entry) and a restart of US exports post-tariff — persistent above-industry gain, though no explicit percentage share figures are given on the calls.
SHAREGAIN.quote: KEI is the first Indian company to supply several projects of extra high-voltage cables, 330 kV cables to Australia... We have expanded our reach to Caribbean islands

CULTURE.rationale: Guidance given in Q1 FY26 (18%, later 'more than 20%') was delivered at 20.66% for FY26, and the Sanand delays were disclosed promptly and specifically on the Q2 call (4 months Phase 1, 9 months Phase 2, with reasons) rather than buried; leadership is stable promoter-led (Anil Gupta CMD FY2021 to current) with a conservative balance sheet — Rs.203 cr borrowings against Rs.1,048 cr net cash.
CULTURE.quote: historically, we've done a very good job in meeting our guidance

MOATTEST.rationale: The EHV end shows a concrete replication barrier — multi-year utility qualification (only Indian firm in the National Grid UK 400 kV framework) plus a 158-metre vertical CV tower that management says no architect, consultant or contractor had experience building — but the majority LT cable and house-wire business is a scale/distribution game a well-funded entrant can and is rebuilding.
MOATTEST.quote: the complexities faced in construction of vertical tower of 158 meter... no architects or consultants or contractors had much experience in building making this type of construction

RECURRING.rationale: The RTA model is a front-end mandate win followed by an annuity fee stream on the installed base — AMCs, 10,500+ corporate issuers, folios, AIFs and pension subscribers all bill recurringly, and management tracks client counts and installed base as the core growth metric across all four FY26/FY27 calls. Wins compound: new AMC mandates (Nuvama, Monarch, 4 in FY26) and 499 fund-manager additions at Ascent convert into ongoing AUM-linked revenue.
RECURRING.quote: We crossed 10,500 total corporate client as of 31st March. We aim to cross -- we aim to get to close to 11,500 into this upcoming year

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: The paying customer is the asset manager or issuer itself; there is no professional intermediary recommending KFin to a separate paying end-customer, and no trade-training or channel-relationship programme is discussed on any of the four calls.

TOLLROAD.rationale: Structurally a rational duopoly supplying a mission-critical, low-cost-share service — registrar/transfer agency, and management describes orchestrating client transitions in and rarely out — but the pattern's 'customers pay without negotiating' test is contradicted by the April 2025 pricing discounts and the telescopic yield compression discussed in Q4 FY26.
TOLLROAD.quote: part of that was the pricing discounts that were given in t he month of April 2025

LOWPRICE.rationale: Management repeatedly positions its right to win on cost — 'frugal engineering' and cost optimisation offered to asset managers — and it does run high EBITDA margins on an asset-light base, but the calls disclose no itemised cost culture or savings programme, and margins compressed rather than being defended by volume/turns.
LOWPRICE.quote: our right to win has been consolidating both in terms of the cost optimization we are able to offer and render to the various asset managers

PRICING.rationale: The last-12-months evidence points the other way: domestic mutual fund yields fell ~2.6% in Q3 FY26 on passive/metal-ETF mix, and Q4 FY26 explicitly attributed AUM growing 21% against revenue up only ~11% to prior-year pricing discounts. This is price deflation, the pattern's stated opposite.
PRICING.quote: the domestic mutual fund yield has slightly come down by about 2.6%

BRAND.rationale: There is clear institutional reputation — 60% win rate on new AMC mandates, ~80% by market cap of the quarter's IPOs, and reputation-adjacent proof points like the ESG score rise to 63 and Bitsight 810 — but no heritage story, A&P spend or premium pricing, and the brand demonstrably does not command price.
BRAND.quote: nearly 80% by market cap of all the IPOs that have happened in the quarter that had gone by have all been orchestrated by KFin Technologies

INNOVATION.rationale: Management claims a quarterly cadence of new product deployment and credits technology for pension share gains, but no R&D spend, share of industry R&D, or revenue attribution to named launches is disclosed on any of the four calls — and the innovation has not translated into pricing power.
INNOVATION.quote: Nearly every quarter, we try to develop and make innovative solutions, which not just in India, in fact, many parts of the w orld have not seen.

FORWARD.rationale: KFin is a B2B service provider to AMCs, issuers and fund managers; the calls contain no discussion of own stores, franchising, licensing or direct-to-end-customer channels.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Explicit, quantified share gains across every line and against named benchmarks: mutual fund AAUM share 30% (2020) to 32.7%, SIP share ~37%, Issuer Solutions above 50-52% of Nifty 500 by market cap, 38% AIF share, and pensions growing 34% versus industry 11% to take second place from the incumbent — plus international expansion via Ascent growing ~200% y/y.
SHAREGAIN.quote: The overall market share of AAUM for KFintech continues to rise from about 30% in 2020 to now 32.7%.

CULTURE.rationale: Leadership is stable (Nadella/Mathur across all four calls) and the diversification promise made four years ago has visibly been delivered — non-domestic-MF revenue now near 40% — and management discloses bad news plainly (flat PAT, yield compression, Issuer Solutions base effect, margin dilution from Ascent). Against that, EBITDA/PAT growth of 5-7% has lagged the repeated 20%+ top-line framing, and the one-year lens does not let me test through-cycle capital allocation.
CULTURE.quote: there was a fair amount of skepticism in terms of if it is possible to orchestrate several such large businesses, but lo and behold, in a matter of four years, a near 40% of the revenue comes from businesses which are beyond

MOATTEST.rationale: A newcomer would need SEBI registration, decades of accumulated folio/investor data, and would have to persuade AMCs and 10,500 issuers to migrate a mission-critical record-keeping system — the calls describe KFin orchestrating transitions in, not out, and near-universal connection to Indian financial-asset investors. That is a two-player market with data scale and switching risk that money alone cannot rebuild quickly.
MOATTEST.quote: Nearly every individual in India who has invested in a financial asset class has some connection with KFin Technologies

RECURRING.rationale: The four FY26 calls discuss bed capacity, ARPOB, occupancy and EBITDA ramp-up of new units, but contain no discussion of recurring licence/subscription/AMC streams, attach or renewal rates, or customer advances as a funding source.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Doctors are the de facto middlemen — the calls repeatedly attribute performance to named clinicians and their teams (transplant programmes led by Dr. Sandeep Attawar, Dr. Uma Maheshwara Rao, Dr. Venugopal), and referral-driven complex work at new units, though the calls never describe channel/referral programmes or trade training as a deliberate lock-in mechanism.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: 100 Heart n lung transplants were done in 2025 under the leadership of Dr Sandeep Attawar and his team.

TOLLROAD.rationale: KIMS is the payer-facing service provider, not a small-ticket critical input; the Q1 FY26 call shows its economics hostage to insurance and corporate empanelment rather than to non-negotiable pricing.
TOLLROAD.quote: The ramp-up at Nashik has been a little slow because of tie-up from insurance -- delaying tie-up from insurance and corporate.

LOWPRICE.rationale: The founding mission of affordable, accessible care in tier-2/3 towns is restated in these calls (complex care such as transplants brought to small towns), but the FY26 calls show no cost-obsession culture or itemised savings — margins fell from 26.6% to 21.1% on expansion drag rather than being defended by a cost machine.
LOWPRICE.quote: excellent medical care and latest technology is now available at tier 2 and 3 centres wherever KIMS is there. Even organ transplants are taking place at these small towns which was unheard of before.

PRICING.rationale: FY26 shows ARPOB +14% and ARPP +11.4% year-on-year with IP volumes +15.4% and OP +25.4% — realisation rising alongside volumes — but management attributes the gains to case-mix (transplants, robotics) and new-market mix rather than to explicit price increases, and even guides to some ARPOB normalisation in Karnataka.
PRICING.quote: Average revenue per operating bed grew by 14% on year-on-year basis... IP and OP volumes grew by 15.4% and 25.4% respectively

BRAND.rationale: Twenty-five years of heritage from the first Nellore hospital, and new units convert reputation into fast ramp (Thane doing 1,000+ surgeries in under six months, INR9 crores of monthly revenue ahead of expectation), but the brand is regional and demonstrably not portable without effort — Nashik's ramp lagged and management concedes the strength is clinical rather than consumer-marketing led.
BRAND.quote: The unit conducted more than 1,000 surgeries in less than 6 months, a testimony to the growing goodwill.

INNOVATION.rationale: Each recent call names new clinical technology with real firsts — Tulsa Pro, MRgFUS, South India's first Gamma Knife, Medtronic robotic spine guidance, an XR lab — but this is purchased equipment adoption, not proprietary R&D, and no R&D spend or revenue attribution is disclosed.
INNOVATION.quote: Launch of India's first Tulsa Pro for Prostate Cancer care treatment... Launch of South India's first Gamma Knife for brain tumours

FORWARD.rationale: Not applicable in the evidence: KIMS already owns and operates its hospitals; the calls contain no franchising, licensing or D2C discussion beyond the Chennai land arrangement, which is a lease-and-operate structure rather than forward integration.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Volume-led expansion is real and rapid — revenue +28.2% in FY26, 7 hospitals launched in 2025, 25 centres across 5 states — but management never cites market-share numbers or names competitors, and the share is being bought with heavy capex that cut PAT from INR415 crores to INR242 crores.
SHAREGAIN.quote: Total revenue of INR 3,931 crore, a growth of 28.2% on year-on-year basis... EBITDA margin of 21.1% versus 26.6% in Financial Year '25.

CULTURE.rationale: Founder-family leadership (Bhaskar Rao and Abhinay Bollineni continuously through FY22–FY26) discloses the margin damage plainly and gives dated breakeven guidance that has broadly held — Thane and Kannur ramped as promised — but Bangalore/Electronic City breakeven slipped from the Q1 guide to end-Q3 FY27, CFO turnover occurred in FY24, and the equity-funded QIP disclosed in Q4 shows expansion outrunning internal funding.
CULTURE.quote: Expansions necessarily involve heavy expenditure and it strains the profits in the initial phase. Likewise, the profit of the company for the year is impacted

MOATTEST.rationale: Genuine replication barriers exist in the quaternary programmes — 10,000+ brain tumour surgeries, 100 heart-lung and 430+ renal transplants in one year, decades of clinician assembly — which a funded newcomer could not rebuild quickly; but the calls also show the model is fundamentally replicable bed capacity, with rivals expanding into the same geographies and KIMS itself entering new cities on leased land.
MOATTEST.quote: we accomplished an important milestone of completing 10,000-plus successful brain tumor surgeries at KIMS

RECURRING.rationale: The May 2025 call describes service and framework contracts covering entire customer rigs — including servicing and supplying spares for competitors' pumps — which is a genuine recurring stream off the installed base, but across all four FY26 calls management never quantifies attach rates, AMC/service revenue share, renewals, or deferred revenue as a funding source.
RECURRING.quote: framework contracts, which allow us to now look after total rigs that not only have our pumps, but everyone else's pumps. So the Service contracts that we are taking, which allow us to supply spare parts for all kinds of equipment

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Domestic retail and JJM/KUSUM volumes go entirely through a multi-generational dealer channel that management deliberately protects, but these dealers are distributors reselling to end users rather than experts prescribing the product, and no trade-training programme is described in any of the four calls.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: we do not take any orders directly from the state government or the central government... We do this with our dealers. These dealers are long-term dealers working with us for many generations. Some of them are with us for 4 generations.

TOLLROAD.rationale: Efficiency certification language recurs (BEE 4/5-star, ecolabel, European Minimum Efficiency Index) and pumps are mission-critical to power, oil & gas and marine customers, but the business is largely tender-driven where the company concedes it must be lowest bidder — the opposite of a niche supplier customers pay without negotiating.
TOLLROAD.quote: we always need to be L1 in these orders, right, because it's tender based

LOWPRICE.rationale: Management positions on efficiency, lowest life-cycle cost and premium realisation rather than low price plus scale; cost work discussed (foundry SAP ERP, waste identification) is framed as efficiency recovery after a disruption, not a hard-to-copy low-cost culture, and FY26 EBITDA margin fell from 15.2% to 13.7% on flat revenue.
LOWPRICE.quote: we do get premiums for our orders even against multinational companies who don't have such products

PRICING.rationale: In May 2026 Sanjay Kirloskar claims premiums versus multinationals on life-cycle-cost and efficiency grounds, and commercial terms are strict (advances, LCs, cash retail), but no explicit price increases without volume loss are cited, tender business is L1-driven, and FY26 margins moderated on mix and operating leverage.
PRICING.quote: customers have started understanding lowest life cycle cost... And therefore, we do get premiums for our orders even against multinational companies

BRAND.rationale: The Kirloskar name carries genuine heritage — an old company with four-generation dealer relationships and a Government of India 'Appliance of the Year' recognition in FY26 — but across the four calls there is no A&P spend, no distributor-leverage economics and no premium-plus-share-gain proof, and FY26 domestic revenue actually declined 3%.
BRAND.quote: the Government of India itself recognized one of our products as the Appliance of the Year

INNOVATION.rationale: New-product cadence is real and named across the window — BEE 5-star/4-star retail pumps, ecolabel series, FGD and strategic-sector pumps, IoT/AR-VR, and canned motor pumps breaking a two-player American hold on retail petroleum — but R&D spend is never disclosed or shown growing, and mid-teens EBITDA margins are not the high-gross-margin engine the pattern describes.
INNOVATION.quote: we are dealing with two monopolistic American players. So we were able to break through there in the market... These are a type of canned motor pumps that we have made.

FORWARD.rationale: The four calls in the window discuss the dealer/distribution channel and tender business but say nothing about own stores, franchising, royalties or D2C economics, so there is no basis to judge this pattern either way.
